findings.title: Materials' forward lens is a bet on a 103 percent earnings surge
findings.body: Materials sits at the 21st percentile forward but the 76th percentile trailing, a 55-point gap that is the widest in the table. The forward multiple is 51 percent below trailing, implying analysts expect reported earnings to more than double next year — an extraordinary underwriting at the 21st percentile of its own five-year range.

findings.title: Energy's forward multiple is far cheaper than its trailing record
findings.body: Energy trades at the 34th percentile forward versus the 82nd percentile trailing, a 48-point gap that is the second-largest here. The forward multiple is 39 percent below trailing, implying a 63 percent earnings jump is priced in — yet the sector has been getting cheaper for a month straight, a disconnect between the valuation and the implied growth.

findings.title: Health Care's forward multiple is at a five-year extreme
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E of 20.45 sits at the 100th percentile of its own five-year range, up 18 points in a month, while its trailing multiple is only at the 87th percentile. The 47 percent compression between the two lenses implies an 87 percent earnings surge is being priced in, a level of optimism that has no precedent in the sector's recent history.
